Fluency and property-based reasoning with multiplication/division facts directly supports the multiplicative reasoning the ratio standard names, so proficiency in the second standard supports likely success in the first; the reverse support is not evidenced. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same grain, same rank 0) under Strand 1: NUMBER / Sub-strand 2: Number Operations, so direction rests on statement content rather than rank. The second SFI (B4.1.2.1.1, under Content Standard B4.1.2.1 'Recall basic multiplication fact up to 12 × 12') is the foundational determination of the basic multiplication facts themselves, with exemplars using concrete arrays of straws. The first SFI (B4.1.2.2.1, under B4.1.2.2) substantively extends this: learners apply mental mathematics strategies and number properties (skip counting from a known fact, doubling/halving, patterns in the 9s facts, repeated doubling) and extend to related division facts. Deriving unknown facts from 'a known fact' and generating related division facts presupposes command of the basic multiplication facts, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. Same-rank direction is supported by the derived-from-known-fact wording and the fact-to-strategy/division extension, not merely by shared code prefix, page proximity, or LC token overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Content Standards in the Number strand (identity scope grade=basic 5|strand=number): B5.1.2.2 covers multiplication of 2- or 3-digit numbers, while B5.1.5.1 covers understanding percentage of a given number (indicator excerpts reference determining the percentage of a given quantity limited to 2-digit whole numbers and benchmark percentages from common fractions). There is genuine conceptual coherence — multiplicative computation with multi-digit whole numbers is reinforced when finding a percentage of a quantity — but the evidence shows two distinct topics at the same canonical rank (BASIC 5, rank gap 0) with no statement of dependency, and the nomination signals are weak (shared code prefix 'b5.1' and generic stem tokens such as 'demonstrate', 'understanding', 'number'). That is insufficient substantive evidence for a same-rank developmental direction, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Both endpoints have unresolved ancestry and truncated source evidence (26 and 28 omitted items), so no hierarchy or sub-strand placement was used and the judgment rests only on trustworthy statement text, codes, and coordinates.
